title: Gender, diversity & inclusion with G Sabini-Roberts

sentences.en: So when we are working in mental health, there can feel like a lot of different issues that we need to be aware of.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们在心理健康领域工作时，可能会觉得有许多不同的问题需要我们去关注。

sentences.en: And it can feel like a very quick paced, quick moving beast really to get our heads around and how best to understand the broad variety of people that we work with
sentences.zh: 要真正理解我们所合作的广泛人群，并跟上这个节奏极快、不断变化的领域，可能会让人觉得像是在应付一个快速移动的庞然大物，

sentences.zh: 而他们的独特需求很可能与我们个人和职业上的需求有所不同。

sentences.en: And one of the recent very important debates and themes that have been raised in the media, but also in mental health, has been that of gender and diversity.
sentences.zh: 最近在媒体以及心理健康领域被提出的一项非常重要且备受关注的辩论和主题，就是关于性别与多样性的问题。

sentences.en: And I'm delighted to be able to welcome my guest today so that we can all think about how to understand more about these important issues

sentences.en: and how we might be able to make changes in the way that we do things in our personal and professional practice
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何在个人和专业实践中改变做事方式，

sentences.en: to better be inclusive and to help other people know how open to conversations we are in this area and how we strive to help people feel understood, validated and heard and seen.
sentences.zh: 从而更好地做到包容，并让其他人知道我们在这一领域是多么愿意倾听和交流，我们如何努力帮助人们感受到被理解、被认可、被倾听和被看见。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to today's episode of the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听今天的《有志心理学家播客》。

sentences.en: I am thrilled to be introducing you to G Sabini Roberts.
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴向大家介绍G·萨比尼·罗伯茨（G Sabini Roberts）。

sentences.en: Hi, G.
sentences.zh: 嗨，G。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: So there's a number of reasons I wanted to talk to you in today's episode
sentences.zh: 今天想和你聊聊有很多原因，

sentences.en: because you're just a really interesting character to get to know.
sentences.zh: 因为你真的是一个非常有趣的、值得了解的人物。

sentences.en: So we met on socials and I've been following your work for a while and you're really inspiring for a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们在社交媒体上相识，我关注你的工作有一段时间了，在很多方面你都非常具有启发性。

sentences.en: By trade, you're a brand specialist, sort of doing branding and logos and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你的老本行是品牌专家，主要从事品牌设计、标志设计之类的工作。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That is right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The original business, 11 years old now, is graphic design with a very definite brand specialism.
sentences.zh: 最初的业务已经有11年的历史了，主要做平面设计，且有着非常明确的品牌专业方向。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But you definitely have a more modern twist on the way you work and the topics that you talk about.
sentences.zh: 但你的工作方式以及你谈论的主题绝对有一种更现代的风格。

sentences.en: And that's really what I want to talk with you and to our audience about today.
sentences.zh: 这正是我今天想和你以及我们的听众探讨的话题。

sentences.en: So originally, I wanted to talk to you for a little bit of help, really, a little bit of guidance
sentences.zh: 所以最初我想找你，是希望得到一点帮助和指导，

sentences.en: for how we can be really inclusive in modern mental health services, for thinking about diversity and gender and all stuff along those lines.
sentences.zh: 探讨我们如何在现代心理健康服务中真正做到包容，如何思考多样性、性别以及所有相关的话题。

sentences.en: What's your best advice for how we can do things better in modern mental health services, G?
sentences.zh: G，对于我们如何在现代心理健康服务中做得更好，你有什么最好的建议吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think based on the conversation you and I have already had,
sentences.zh: 嗯，基于你和我已经有过的交流，

sentences.en: what we really want to talk about is confidence and comfort in being able to talk about these things.
sentences.zh: 我们真正想谈的是在能够谈论这些事情时的自信和坦然。

sentences.en: So just in terms of background, I'm queer, I'm non-binary, trans, I use they, them pronouns, and I have been queer my whole life.
sentences.zh: 从背景上讲，我是酷儿（queer）、非二元性别者、跨性别者，我使用的是they/them代词，我一辈子都是酷儿。

sentences.en: And so as well as the branding business in the last few years, I've been doing a lot more diversity inclusion work,
sentences.zh: 因此，除了过去几年的品牌业务外，我还做了更多多元化和包容性的工作，

sentences.en: which, as you will find when you speak to most people who are LGBTQ, we end up inadvertently delivering awareness, training, information, being the go-to voice
sentences.zh: 正如你和大多数LGBTQ人士交谈时会发现的那样，我们最终往往会在无意中提供意识培训、信息，成为首选的代言人，

sentences.en: because we're the only gay that somebody knows it, for example.
sentences.zh: 因为我们可能是某人认识的唯一一个同性恋者，举个例子。

sentences.en: We all do that anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们无论如何都在做这些。

sentences.en: That's something we do for free every day of the week.
sentences.zh: 这是我们每周七天都在免费做的事情。

sentences.en: However, a few years ago, we started offering that, myself and a couple of partners, started offering that on a professional basis as well.
sentences.zh: 然而，几年前，我和几个合伙人开始以专业的方式提供这项服务。

sentences.en: So I have that slant to things too, but I'm very much an LGBTQ specialist within that.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这方面也有所涉足，但我很大程度上是其中的LGBTQ专家。

sentences.en: So really, I think the biggest question for most people seems to be, how do I get it right?
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我认为对大多数人来说最大的问题似乎是：我该如何做对？

sentences.en: If I'm faced with a trans person, as an example, how do I speak with them, refer to their past,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果我面对一个跨性别者，我该如何与他们交谈、提及他们的过去、

sentences.en: talk to them in a way that enables them to access whatever it is we're trying to access in a way that includes them and doesn't put up barriers.
sentences.zh: 以一种能够让他们获得我们试图获取的资源的方式与他们交谈，这种方式要包容他们，而不是设置障碍。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is that where, do you think that kind of thing is what will be useful for people here?
sentences.zh: 你认为这类事情对这里的听众会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 是的，拜托了。

sentences.en: OK, so the first aspect of this is to recognise that when it comes to gender identity, particularly gender identity is an identity.
sentences.zh: 好的，这方面的第一个方面是要认识到，当谈到性别认同，特别是性别认同，它是一种身份认同。

sentences.en: It's how you feel in your head.
sentences.zh: 这是你在脑海中的感受。

sentences.en: Your gender is between your ears, not between your legs is a brilliant quote.
sentences.zh: “你的性别在你的双耳之间，而不是在你的双腿之间”，这是一句精彩的名言。

sentences.en: That's a Charles Bono magical quote, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 这是查尔斯·博诺（Charles Bono）的一句神奇名言，但它是真的。

sentences.en: So when we're talking from a psychological point of view, it is very much, it's an identity
sentences.zh: 所以当我们从心理学的角度来谈论时，它在很大程度上是一种身份认同，

sentences.en: that is owned and it does not necessarily correlate in any way, shape or form with somebody's
sentences.zh: 这是个人所拥有的，它不一定与某人的生理、生物学、解剖学、荷尔蒙、染色体等构成生物学性别的所有因素有任何形式或方式的关联。

sentences.en: physiology, biology, anatomy, hormones, chromosomes, all of the things that go into making a biological sex.
sentences.zh: 承认这一点很重要，因为某人走进房间，你看着他们，就把他们归类为一个特定的性别。

sentences.en: And it's important to acknowledge that because somebody may walk into a room and you look at them and you clock them as a particular gender.
sentences.zh: 但在你实际询问他们是否以这种方式认同之前，你并不知道情况是否如此。

sentences.en: And you do not know that that's the case until you've actually asked them if that's how they identify.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们有时很容易因为妄加揣测而无意中说错话、做错事。

sentences.en: And this is why it's sometimes really easy to inadvertently put our foot in it because we make assumptions.
sentences.zh: 首先要认识到我们生活在一个严重以性别划分的社会中。

sentences.en: And that's the first thing is to recognise that we live in a massively gendered society.
sentences.zh: 我们把从工作到情绪、再到时尚的一切都按性别进行了划分，无一例外。

sentences.en: We have gendered everything from jobs to emotions to fashion, all of it.
sentences.zh: 我们有着这样的假设：看到这个，我们就认为它是男性的；看到那个，

sentences.en: We have assumptions of we see this and we assume male, we see that.
sentences.zh: 我们就认为它是女性的。

sentences.en: We assume female.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想要确保在任何时候遇到新面孔或新状况时，

sentences.en: And that's the thing that we need to unpackage if we are going to make sure that at any moment
sentences.zh: 都能意识到他们的性别认同可能并不像我们因为受生活环境条件限制而想当然的那样，那么这就是我们需要剖析和打破的东西。

sentences.en: when we meet somebody new or we encounter somebody new, we are aware that they may not identify in the way we're going to assume that they will because we've been conditioned by
sentences.zh: 这就是第一点。

sentences.en: the world that we live in.
sentences.zh: 因此，随时你可能会说，哦，是的，你看到走廊尽头的那位女士了吗？

sentences.en: That's the first thing.
sentences.zh: 那个人立刻……

sentences.en: So anytime you might say, oh, yes, do you see that lady down the end of the corridor?
sentences.zh: 你并不知道那个人可能穿着裙子，但他们会把自己认同为女士吗？

sentences.en: That's the person immediately.
sentences.zh: 他们会把自己认同为女士吗？

sentences.en: You do not know that person may be wearing a dress, but would they identify as a lady?
sentences.zh: 即使他们认同为女性，这也完全关乎认识到我们使用的语言可能分量很重，并以此作为意识的起点。

sentences.en: Would they identify as a lady?
sentences.zh: 我们可以，我们可以围绕这一点做出调整。

sentences.en: Even if they identified as a woman, it's all about recognising the language we use can be very weighted and being conscious as a starting point.
sentences.zh: 近年来，围绕代词、人们分享自己的代词以及询问代词，已经有很多讨论了。

sentences.en: And we can, we can work around that.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: So there's been a lot of conversations over recent years around pronouns and people sharing their pronouns and asking for pronouns.
sentences.zh: 我曾遇到过这样的人，他们说：我看到其他人分享他们的代词，但我是一个男人。

sentences.en: And that is a really significant thing.
sentences.zh: 我显然是个男人。

sentences.en: I have encountered people who have said, I see other people sharing their pronouns, but I'm a man.
sentences.zh: 人们认为我是个男人，因此我不需要分享我的代词，因为这是显而易见的。

sentences.en: I'm clearly a man.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能反思这一点，我们就可以说：如果你是一个经常被你周围的世界、被你每天在街上遇到的人看作你自己所知的那个性别的人，那么你就拥有性别特权。

sentences.en: People perceive me as a man and therefore I don't need to share them because it's obvious.
sentences.zh: 而我们要求人们在电子邮件签名、视频通话的身份标签等地方添加代词，

sentences.en: And if we can reflect that back, we can say, well, if you are somebody who is regularly perceived
sentences.zh: 是因为我们认识到，并非所有人都会将自己认同为你从屏幕上看到他们或在任何环境中遇到他们时所假设的性别。

sentences.en: by the world around you, by the people you encounter every day in the street as the gender that you know yourself to be, then you have gender privilege.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: And what we are asking people to do by adding their pronouns to their email signatures or their
sentences.zh: 通过添加我们自己的代词，我们有助于将这一过程正常化，将其作为我们所有人普遍认同方式的一部分。

sentences.en: ID tags on their video calls and things like that, is we are recognising that not all people identify
sentences.zh: 首先，这意味着你的性别总是会被正确称呼，因为你的代词就在那里。

sentences.en: as the gender you may assume them to be when you see them on screen or encounter them in whatever setting you're in.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着两件事。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 第一，你会遇到这样的人，他们会问：你为什么要把代词写在上面？

sentences.en: And by adding our own, we help to normalise the process of including that as part of how we all generally identify.
sentences.zh: 你留着胡子，声音低沉。

sentences.en: First off, it means that you're always going to be gendered correctly because your pronouns are right there.
sentences.zh: 你显然是个男人。而你会说：实际上，并非所有拥有这些特征的人都是男人。

sentences.en: But it also means that two things.
sentences.zh: 我在表明我是。

sentences.en: One, you'll encounter people who say, why do you put your pronouns on there?
sentences.zh: 而且我还在含蓄地告诉世界，告诉任何可能遇到我的性别多元化人士：我是安全的，我懂的。

sentences.en: You've got a beard and a deep voice.
sentences.zh: 我考虑过这些事情，并且我认识到，作为一个拥有性别特权的人，

sentences.en: You're clearly a man says, well, actually not all people who maybe have those features are men.
sentences.zh: 我可以开始将这种询问代词的过程正常化，将确认个人代词作为正常日常文化的一部分。

sentences.en: And I'm making it clear that I am.
sentences.zh: 这减轻了性别多元化人群的压力，让他们不必总是去说：“不好意思，我能纠正你一下吗？”

sentences.en: And I'm also subtly telling the world, telling any person who is gender diverse that may encounter me, that I'm safe, I get it.
sentences.zh: 每当你不得不这样做时，它对一个人心理健康的负面影响是巨大的，

sentences.en: I've thought about this stuff and I recognise that as somebody who has gender privilege,
sentences.zh: 特别是当你一天要做33次的时候。

sentences.en: I can start to normalise this process of asking for pronouns, making identifying one's own pronouns part of normal everyday culture.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过在这种事情上采取积极主动的态度，我们开始帮助减轻这种压力。

sentences.en: It takes the pressure off gender diverse people to always be the people who are saying, excuse me, can I just correct you there?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是需要承认的第一点：我们并不知道。我知道这具体关乎性别，

sentences.en: Which every time you have to do that, we've got that, the negative impact that that has on somebody's mental wellbeing is significant,
sentences.zh: 我们可能希望以更广泛的方式来谈论多样性和包容性，但这是我被问得最多的重要问题之一。

sentences.en: especially when you're doing it 33 times a day.
sentences.zh: 所有这些关于代词的事情到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So we start to help to take that pressure by being proactive in that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: So that's, that's the first point to acknowledge is we don't know, I know that's specifically gender,
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: and we may want to talk about diversity and inclusion in a, in a more broad way, but that is one of the most significant questions I get asked.
sentences.zh: 我知道，比如在领英（LinkedIn）上，因为它提供让你选择代词的功能，所以我已经设置了。

sentences.en: What, what's all this pronouns stuff about?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，虽然我没有胡子，

sentences.en: And that is what it's about.
sentences.zh: 但我留着长发，而且经常穿裙子。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 因此，我以前不一定会在类似这样的地方想过要写上：玛丽安·特伦特博士，she/her，这会是我的代词，对吧？

sentences.en: And little things like this just help to alleviate that a bit, and just show that all families go.

sentences.en: And what we found to be brilliant is the way that people have jumped on this as a way to start having those conversations.

sentences.en: If you inadvertently misgender somebody or use the incorrect name or title, there's a really easy answer.

sentences.en: That's the really key thing.

sentences.en: somebody about their heritage.

sentences.en: I got it all wrong.

sentences.en: And I'm really sorry.
